reporting.basis: Actual results, from the Annual Financial Report filed with the Illinois Comptroller
reporting.scope: County governmental and enterprise funds, including the sheriff, jail, courts and county highways; pension trusts and money the county collector holds for other governments are left out

ledger.description: State-shared income, sales, motor fuel, replacement and gaming taxes

notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended November 30, 2024, as the county reported them in its Annual Financial Report to the Illinois Comptroller. Not a budget.

Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included. The county collector gathers property taxes for every taxing district and pays them over; that money is left out.

Covers the general, special revenue, capital projects, debt service and enterprise (utility) funds. Pension trusts and other fiduciary funds, internal service funds and component units are left out, as are transfers between funds and borrowing.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is bonds, contracts and other long-term debt outstanding at year end (beginning balance plus new debt less debt retired), as reported.
Political money is not scored: no county board and county office candidates of Wabash County reported contributions to the State Board of Elections since 2023.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-18. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for Illinois yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: Police drones
redFlags.detail: The Wabash County Sheriff's Office has one drone according to the 2024 Illinois Freedom from Drone Surveillance Act Report.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS014398, citing Illinois Criminal Justice Information Authority

notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended April 30, 2024, as the city reported them in its Annual Financial Report to the Illinois Comptroller. Not a budget.

Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included. Residents also pay Wabash County and, in most counties, the township they live in; park, library and fire protection districts are separate governments too.

Covers the general, special revenue, capital projects, debt service and enterprise (utility) funds. Pension trusts and other fiduciary funds, internal service funds and component units are left out, as are transfers between funds and borrowing.
Depreciation ($591,790) is left out; capital outlay is counted when paid.
Capital outlay outside utility funds ($457,394) is reported without a function, so it is spread over the city's services in proportion to their spending.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is bonds, contracts and other long-term debt outstanding at year end (beginning balance plus new debt less debt retired), as reported.

Political money is not scored: no candidates for mayor or village president, council or board, clerk and other local offices of City of Mount Carmel reported contributions to the State Board of Elections since 2023.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Cameras: 3 license-plate cameras are mapped inside City of Mount Carmel's borders in OpenStreetMap (3 made by Flock Safety), not counting cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies. Flock cameras count as a red flag whoever runs them. Other brands count only when the government is the recorded operator, since many have no operator recorded.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-18. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals and corporate tax breaks have not been checked for Illinois yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: Flock camera network
redFlags.detail: 3 Flock Safety license-plate cameras are mapped inside City of Mount Carmel's borders in OpenStreetMap. Flock cameras photograph every passing car and feed a search network shared with police agencies across the country. Who runs each camera is not recorded; cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies are not counted.

redFlags.detail: The Mount Carmel Police Department has one drones according to the 2024 Illinois Freedom from Drone Surveillance Act Report.
